question.text: Consider the following data sets: \[ x = \big\{ 2, \: 1, \: -1 \big\},\qquad y = \big\{ 15, \: 12, \: 9 \big\} \] You're given that $\overline{x}=\dfrac23,$ $\overline{y}=12,$ $\sigma_x \approx 1.247,$ and $\sigma_y \approx 2.449.$ Calculate the corresponding linear correlation coefficient. Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
question.explanation:
The (population) linear correlation coefficient of the data sets $x=\big\{ x_1,x_2, \ldots, x_n \big\}$ and $y=\big\{ y_1,y_2, \ldots, y_n \big\}$ is given by

\[ \rho(x,y) = \dfrac{\textrm{Cov}(x,y)}{\sigma_x \cdot \sigma_y} \]

where $\textrm{Cov}(x,y)$ is the covariance, and $\sigma_x$ and $\sigma_y$ are the standard deviations of the data sets.

First, we need to compute the covariance:

\begin{align*} \textrm{Cov}(x,y) &=\dfrac{1}{n} \sum\limits_{i=1}^n (x_i - \overline{x})(y_i - \overline{y}) \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{1}{3} \Bigg[ \left(2-\dfrac23\right)(15-12) + \left(1-\dfrac23\right)(12-12) + \left(-1-\dfrac23\right)(9-12)\Bigg] \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{1}{3} \Bigg[ \left(\dfrac43\right)(3) + \left(\dfrac13\right)(0) + \left(-\dfrac53\right)(-3)\Bigg] \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{1}{3} \big[ 4 + 0 +5 \big] \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{1}{3} \cdot 9 \\[5pt] &=3 \end{align*}

Finally, we use the formula. This gives

\begin{align*} \rho(x,y) &= \dfrac{\textrm{Cov}(x,y)}{\sigma_x \cdot \sigma_y} \\[5pt] &\approx \dfrac{3}{1.247 \cdot 2.449} \\[5pt] &\approx 0.98 \end{align*}

rounded to $2$ decimal places.

exampleAnswers.title: Computing the Linear Correlation Coefficient Using the Expanded Formula

question.text:
The data sets $x$ and $y$ have the following properties:

\[ S_{xx} = 41, \qquad S_{xy} = -39, \qquad S_{yy} = 61 \]

Calculate the corresponding linear correlation coefficient. Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
question.explanation:
Recall the definitions of $S_{xx},$ $S_{xy},$ and $S_{yy}$ for the data sets $x=\big\{ x_1,x_2, \ldots, x_n \big\}$ and $y=\big\{ y_1,y_2, \ldots, y_n \big\}{:}$

\[ S_{xx} = \sum\limits_{i=1}^n (x_i - \overline{x})^2, \qquad S_{xy} = \sum\limits_{i=1}^n (x_i - \overline{x}) (y_i - \overline{y}), \qquad S_{yy} = \sum\limits_{i=1}^n (y_i - \overline{y})^2 \]

The linear correlation coefficient $\rho$ of the data sets $x$ and $y$ is given by

\[ \rho(x,y) = \dfrac{\textrm{Cov}(x,y)}{\sigma_x \cdot \sigma_y} = \dfrac{S_{xy}}{\sqrt{S_{xx} \cdot S_{yy}}}. \]

Using the formula, we get

\begin{align*} \rho(x,y) &= \dfrac{(-39)}{\sqrt{41} \cdot \sqrt{61}} \\[5pt] &\approx -\dfrac{39}{6.403\,124 \cdot 7.810\,250} \\[5pt] &\approx -0.78 \end{align*}

rounded to $2$ decimal places.

question.text: Consider the following data sets: \[ x = \big\{ 13, \: 4, \: 10\big\},\qquad y = \big\{ 0, \: -3, \: 9 \big\} \] You are given that $\overline{x}=9$ and $\overline{y}=2.$ Calculate the corresponding linear correlation coefficient. Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
question.explanation:
The linear correlation coefficient $\rho$ of the data sets $x=\big\{ x_1,x_2, \ldots, x_n \big\}$ and $y=\big\{ y_1,y_2, \ldots, y_n \big\}$ is given by

\[ \rho(x,y) = \dfrac{\textrm{Cov}(x,y)}{\sigma_x \cdot \sigma_y} = \dfrac{S_{xy}}{\sqrt{S_{xx} \cdot S_{yy}}}. \]

First, we compute the sum in the numerator:

\begin{align*} S_{xy} &= \sum\limits_{i=1}^n (x_i - \overline{x})(y_i - \overline{y}) \\[3pt] &= (13-9)(0-2) + (4-9)(-3-2) + (10-9)(9-2) \\ &= (4)(-2) + (-5)(-5) + (1)(7) \\[5pt] &= -8 +25+7 \\[5pt] &= 24 \end{align*}

Second, we compute the sums in the denominator:

\begin{align*} S_{xx} &= \sum\limits_{i=1}^n (x_i - \overline{x})^2 \\[3pt] &= (13-9)^2 + (4-9)^2 + (10-9)^2 \\[5pt] &= 16+ 25 + 1 \\[5pt] &= 42 \\[10pt] S_{yy} &= \sum\limits_{i=1}^n (y_i - \overline{y})^2 \\[3pt] &= (0-2)^2 + (-3-2)^2 + (9-2)^2 \\[5pt] &= 4+ 25 + 49 \\[5pt] &= 78 \end{align*}

Finally, we use the formula:

\begin{align*} \rho(x,y) &= \dfrac{24}{\sqrt{42} \cdot \sqrt{78}} \\[5pt] &\approx \dfrac{24}{6.480\,741 \cdot 8.831\,761} \\[5pt] &\approx 0.42 \end{align*}

rounded to $2$ decimal places.

question.text: Consider the following data sets: \[ x = \big\{ 5, \: 8, \: 2\big\},\qquad y = \big\{ -1, \: 2, \: 5 \big\} \] You are given that $\overline{x}=5$ and $\overline{y}=2.$ Calculate the corresponding linear correlation coefficient.
question.explanation:
The linear correlation coefficient $\rho$ of the data sets $x=\big\{ x_1,x_2, \ldots, x_n \big\}$ and $y=\big\{ y_1,y_2, \ldots, y_n \big\}$ is given by

\[ \rho(x,y) = \dfrac{\textrm{Cov}(x,y)}{\sigma_x \cdot \sigma_y} = \dfrac{S_{xy}}{\sqrt{S_{xx} \cdot S_{yy}}}. \]

First, we compute the sum in the numerator:

\begin{align*} S_{xy} &= \sum\limits_{i=1}^n (x_i - \overline{x})(y_i - \overline{y}) \\[3pt] &= (5-5)(-1-2) + (8-5)(2-2) + (2-5)(5-2) \\[5pt] &= (0)(-3) + (3)(0) + (-3)(3) \\[5pt] &= 0 +0-9 \\[5pt] &= -9 \end{align*}

Second, we compute the sums in the denominator:

\begin{align*} S_{xx} &= \sum\limits_{i=1}^n (x_i - \overline{x})^2 \\[3pt] &= (5-5)^2 + (8-5)^2 + (2-5)^2 \\[5pt] &= 0 + 9 + 9 \\[5pt] &= 18 \\[10pt] S_{yy} &= \sum\limits_{i=1}^n (y_i - \overline{y})^2 \\[3pt] &= (-1-2)^2 + (2-2)^2 + (5-2)^2\\[5pt] &= 9+ 0 + 9 \\[5pt] &= 18 \end{align*}

Finally, we use the formula:

\begin{align*} \rho(x,y) &= \dfrac{(-9)}{\sqrt{18} \cdot \sqrt{18}} \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{-9}{3\sqrt{2} \cdot 3\sqrt{2}} \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{1}{2} \\[5pt] &= -0.5 \end{align*}

question.text:
An ergonomist investigates $4$ factories. He wants to check the strength of the linear correlation between $x,$ the money spent by factory owners on safety training courses, and $y,$ the number of accidents per year in the factories. The data is shown below.

Money spent (hundreds of $\$$) $10$ $15$ $12$ $23$
Number of accidents $3$ $6$ $5$ $2$

You are given that the means are $\overline{x}=15$ and $\overline{y}=4.$ Which of the following statements are true?

  1. $\rho\approx -0.45$
  2. There is a strong negative correlation between $x$ and $y.$
  3. There is a weak negative correlation between $x$ and $y.$
Hint: $|\rho| > 0.7$ indicates a strong correlation, and $0.3 \leq |\rho| \leq 0.7$ indicates a weak correlation.
question.explanation:
The linear correlation coefficient $\rho$ of the data sets $x=\big\{ x_1,x_2, \ldots, x_n \big\}$ and $y=\big\{ y_1,y_2, \ldots, y_n \big\}$ is given by

\[ \rho(x,y) = \dfrac{\textrm{Cov}(x,y)}{\sigma_x \cdot \sigma_y} = \dfrac{S_{xy}}{\sqrt{S_{xx} \cdot S_{yy}}}. \]

In addition, we have the following rule of thumb:

  • if $|\rho| \gt 0.7,$ the correlation is strong

  • if $0.3\leq |\rho| \leq 0.7,$ the correlation is weak

  • if $|\rho| \lt 0.3,$ then the correlation is negligible

Let's now examine our statements in turn:

  • Statement I is true. To calculate $\rho,$ we first compute the sum in the numerator: \begin{align*} S_{xy} &= \sum\limits_{i=1}^n (x_i - \overline{x})(y_i - \overline{y}) \\[3pt] &= (10-15)(3-4) + (15-15)(6-4) \\[5pt] &\phantom{=} + (12-15)(5-4) + (23-15)(2-4) \\[5pt] &= (-5)(-1) + (0)(2) + (-3)(1) + (8)(-2) \\[5pt] &=5 + 0 - 3 - 16 \\[5pt] &=-14 \end{align*} Second, we compute the sums in the denominator: \begin{align*} S_{xx} &= \sum\limits_{i=1}^n (x_i - \overline{x})^2 \\[3pt] &= (10-15)^2 + (15-15)^2 + (12-15)^2 + (23-15)^2 \\[5pt] &= 25 +0 + 9 + 64\\[5pt] &= 98 \\[10pt] S_{yy} &= \sum\limits_{i=1}^n (y_i - \overline{y})^2 \\[3pt] &= (3-4)^2 + (6-4)^2 + (5-4)^2 + (2-4)^2 \\[5pt] &= 1 + 4 + 1 + 4 \\[5pt] &= 10 \end{align*} Finally, we use the formula: \begin{align*} \rho(x,y) &= \dfrac{-14}{\sqrt{98} \cdot \sqrt{10}} \\[5pt] &\approx -\dfrac{14}{9.899\,495 \cdot 3.162\,278} \\[5pt] &\approx -0.45, \end{align*} rounded to $2$ decimal places.

  • Statement II is false while statement III is true. Since $0.3\leq |\rho| \leq 0.7,$ the correlation is weak. Also, since $\rho$ is negative, the correlation is negative.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."
